name: Vision Transformer (ViT)
analogy: Think of it as cutting a printed candlestick chart into a grid of square tiles, handing the tiles around a table, and letting every person look at every other tile before one reader, holding a summary card, says what pattern the picture shows.

steps.title: Draw the chart as a picture
steps.description: The recent bars are drawn as a candlestick chart image of fixed size, the way a trader would see it on screen. The model works on the picture, not on the table of numbers behind it.
steps.inExample: The last 60 one-minute MNQ bars are drawn as a 224 by 224 pixel candlestick image.

steps.title: Cut the picture into tiles
steps.description: The image is divided into a grid of equal square tiles. Each tile is flattened into a list of pixel values and converted by a learned layer into a compact numeric description.
steps.inExample: With 16 by 16 pixel tiles the image becomes 196 tiles, and the two rightmost columns cover the most recent 8 or so bars.

steps.title: Mark where each tile came from
steps.description: A position signal is added to each tile so the model knows whether it is top left or bottom right, because left to right here means earlier to later. A special summary token is placed at the front to collect the final answer.
steps.inExample: Each of the 196 tiles gets its row and column marker, and a summary token is placed in front, making 197 items.

steps.title: Let every tile look at every other tile
steps.description: Stacked transformer layers use self-attention so each tile can draw on any other tile, near or far. A tile with a long wick can link up with a distant tile showing a similar earlier wick. Several heads look for different relationships at once.
steps.inExample: After 12 layers, the tile holding the latest long lower wick is strongly linked to a tile 30 bars earlier holding a similar wick.

steps.title: Read the answer from the summary token
steps.description: After the final layer the summary token has absorbed what the tiles said. A small output layer turns it into class probabilities, such as which candlestick pattern the picture shows or which direction the next move may take.
steps.inExample: The summary token yields: bullish engulfing 44 percent, hammer 18 percent, no pattern 38 percent.

useFor.example: Labelling a window of MNQ 1-minute bars as a bullish engulfing, hammer or no pattern, as the dashboard's candle vision study does with its 61 patterns.

useFor.task: Learning from how a chart looks
useFor.example: Capturing shapes that are hard to write as indicators, like a staircase of higher lows into a flat top.

useFor.task: Picking up distant relationships on a chart
useFor.example: Linking a double top whose two peaks are 40 bars apart, where a small local filter would see only one peak at a time.
Starting from a model pre-trained on ordinary pictures and fine-tuning it on candlestick images to save training time.

avoidWhen: The numbers behind the chart are available and sufficient; a model on the table of features, such as a gradient boosted tree, avoids throwing away precision by drawing a picture.
You have only a small set of labelled chart images; vision transformers need a lot of data or a pre-trained start, and a small convolutional network tends to do better on little data.
Pixel-exact price levels matter, such as a stop a quarter of a point away; tile and pixel resolution blurs exact prices.

example.scenario: At 10:42 Eastern the last 60 one-minute MNQ bars are drawn as a candlestick image and the model is asked which candle pattern the end of the picture shows.

input.summary: One image of the last 60 bars, broken into 196 tiles, with the ending bars at the right edge.

fields.name: image size
fields.meaning: The size of the drawn chart the model receives.

fields.name: tile size
fields.meaning: How big each square piece of the picture is.

fields.name: number of tiles
fields.meaning: The 14 by 14 grid of tiles the picture is cut into.

fields.name: bars drawn
fields.meaning: How much time the picture covers, one hour.

fields.name: latest close
fields.meaning: The close of the last bar drawn, near the right edge.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The typical high-to-low travel of a recent one-minute bar, which sets the vertical scale of the drawing.

output.summary: Pattern probabilities and where in the picture the model looked.

fields.name: bullish engulfing
fields.meaning: The share of confidence given to the last two bars forming a bullish engulfing pattern.

fields.name: hammer
fields.meaning: The share given to a hammer shape in the last bar.

fields.name: no pattern
fields.meaning: The share given to neither pattern being present.

fields.name: most attended region
fields.meaning: The tiles over the last few bars drew the most attention from the summary token.

example.reading: A 44 percent reading is a lean, not a certain label, and a pattern name is not a forecast. To use it, test whether bars labelled bullish engulfing at this confidence went on to a higher close 6 bars later more often than the base rate on held-out folds, after costs.
